summary: A reply from Rand to RFC 111, which asked sites for implementation schedules. It restates the memo's two goals: realistic schedules, and sharing of techniques that worked. The author had not yet prodded sites because the schedules depend on Telnet, and no Telnet specification was available to everyone.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 130 responds to a request for network implementation schedules. J. Heafner says he will ask sites for schedules after a TELNET specification is available to everyone.

subtitle: A reply explaining why implementation schedules awaited a TELNET specification.

tldr.problem: RFC 111 requested implementation schedules, but the host schedules depended on TELNET and no specification was yet known to everyone.
tldr.mechanism: J. Heafner explains that he will contact site liaisons after a TELNET RFC appears and collect schedules for publication with Alex McKenzie's editing.
tldr.outcome: RFC 130 updates RFC 111 with a response about schedule collection and remote testing.

today: RFC 130 updates RFC 111 with a response about schedules and testing. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces it.

sections.title: The Goals of RFC 111
sections.content:
J. Heafner interprets RFC 111 as having two purposes: to establish realistic implementation schedules and share them with the Network community, and to identify implementation techniques that may help future work.

He says he has not yet contacted host teams because their schedules include TELNET, for which no specification is known to everyone.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier request sought realistic schedules and useful implementation experience. Heafner was waiting for a shared TELNET specification before asking host teams for dates.

sections.title: Collecting and Publishing Schedules
sections.content:
Heafner plans to contact site liaisons after receiving advice that a TELNET RFC will be produced. He and Alex McKenzie agree that schedules should be published as an RFC updating NIC Memo 5767.

Heafner will collect information by phone, mail, or NIC and send it to McKenzie for technical editing and publication. The schedules may refer to the forthcoming Resource Notebook rather than duplicate its information.
sections.plainLanguage: Heafner plans to gather site schedules and pass them to McKenzie for editing. The schedules are intended to update an existing NIC memo.

sections.title: Remote Testing by RAND
sections.content:
Heafner says RAND will assist in testing implementations remotely, as described in RFC 111. He wants first-hand information about schedules and comments on how RAND might help.

The planned testing is short-term and will not go beyond the scope stated in RFC 111.
sections.plainLanguage: RAND planned short-term remote assistance with implementation testing. Heafner asks site liaisons to share schedules and possible testing needs.

references.text: RFC 111, "Pressure from the chairman", the request being answered.
